ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a coordinate plot of a root locus, with the horizontal axis as the real axis σ and the vertical axis as jω. There are four marked points on the negative half of the real axis, whose positions estimated according to the coordinate scale are approximately -7, -4, -2, and -1. The root locus appears on the real axis as two main intervals: approximately from -7 to -4, and approximately from -2 to -1; at the same time, two conjugate branches leave from near the real axis, respectively enter the upper and lower half-planes, and extend roughly in the vertical direction. Reasoning: For the real-axis root locus, use the odd-number rule: when the total number of open-loop poles and zeros to the right of a certain real-axis interval is odd, that interval belongs to the root locus. In order to make the intervals (-7,-4) and (-2,-1) belong to the root locus, while (-4,-2) and (-1,∞) do not belong to the root locus, the four real-axis singularities from left to right should be: pole, zero, pole, pole. Therefore the zero is at s=-4, and the poles are at s=-7, s=-2, and s=-1. Ignoring any positive gain factor, the transfer function is (s+4)/((s+1)(s+2)(s+7)).

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a real-axis root locus with four marked negative-real-axis points and two branches leaving the real axis symmetrically into the upper and lower half-planes. Calibrate the real-axis locations from the axis ticks as approximately -7, -4, -2, and -1. Use the observed real-axis locus portions and the odd-number rule to determine the pole/zero assignment: the interval from -7 to -4 and the interval from -2 to -1 must be locus, so the ordered singularities must be pole, zero, pole, pole. Therefore the zero is at -4 and the poles are at -1, -2, and -7. Write the transfer function as (s+4)/((s+1)(s+2)(s+7)), ignoring an arbitrary positive gain factor.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the locus has four marked real-axis locations and a pair of complex-conjugate branches that head vertically upward and downward, with their asymptote line crossing the real axis near σ=-3. Read the four locations as approximately -7, -4, -2, and -1. Because there are two asymptotic branches, infer that the number of poles exceeds the number of zeros by 2; with four finite singularities, this means three poles and one zero. Use the asymptote centroid formula to decide which marked point is the zero. Trying zero=-4 gives centroid -3, matching the image, while the other choices do not. Thus the zero is at -4 and the poles are at -1, -2, and -7. Set the arbitrary gain to unity and output (s+4)/((s+1)(s+2)(s+7)).
method.CoT_raw: Image description: The plot is a root locus on the σ horizontal axis and jω vertical axis. On the negative real axis there are four marked real-axis locations, read approximately as -7, -4, -2, and -1. The non-real part of the locus consists of a complex-conjugate pair of branches going upward and downward, and these branches tend toward a nearly vertical asymptote whose real-axis crossing is near σ = -3. Reasoning: Since there are two asymptotic branches, the number of poles exceeds the number of zeros by 2. With four finite real singularity locations visible, this implies three poles and one zero. The asymptote centroid is (sum of poles - sum of zeros)/(number of poles - number of zeros). If the zero is at -4 and the poles are at -1, -2, and -7, then the centroid is ((-1) + (-2) + (-7) - (-4))/2 = -6/2 = -3, matching the image. Therefore the zero is at -4 and the poles are at -1, -2, and -7. Taking the arbitrary gain as unity gives the transfer function (s+4)/((s+1)(s+2)(s+7)).
